translations.text: The members of the prophetic community at Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, “Do you not know that today the Lord will take your master away from over you?” He said, “I know that too. Be quiet.”
Fifty men from the prophetic community went and stood opposite them at a distance, while the two of them stood on the bank of the Jordan.

He called to the Lord and said, “Where is the Lord, the God of my master Elijah?” He too struck the waters of the Jordan, and they divided, half to one side and half to the other, and Elisha crossed over.

A woman, one of the wives of the members of the prophetic community, cried out before Elisha and said, “Your servant, my husband, has died. You know that your servant feared the Lord. Now the creditor has come to take my two sons as his slaves.”
After a day, Elisha came and passed through Shiloh. There was a prominent woman there, and she persuaded him to eat a meal. Whenever he passed through, he would turn aside there to eat.
“Let us prepare a small upstairs room for him and put a bed, a table, a chair, and a lampstand there for him. Whenever he comes to us, he can turn aside there.”

Elisha returned to Gilgal, and there was a famine in the land. The members of the prophetic community were sitting before him. He said to his disciple, “Put the large pot on the fire and cook some stew for the prophetic community.”

His attendant said to him, “How can I set this before a hundred men?” Elisha said to him, “Give it to the people so they can eat, for this is what the Lord says: ‘They will eat and have some left over.’”
“Let us go to the Jordan, and let each man cut a beam there. Let us make ourselves a place to live there.” He said, “Go.”
He went with them, and they came to the Jordan and cut down trees.
The king of Israel sent men to the place that the prophet of God had told him about and warned him to beware of. This happened not just once or twice.
Elisha said to them, “This is not the road, and this is not the town. Follow me, and I will take you to the man you are looking for.” He led them to Samaria.

They came and called to the gatekeepers of the town and told them, “We went to the camp of Edom, and there was no one there, nor any sound of a person—only horses tied up, donkeys tied up, and tents just as they were.”
In the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Joram, king of Judah, began to reign.

A horseman went to meet him and said to him, “The king says, ‘Is there peace?’” Jehu said, “What have you to do with peace? Turn around and follow me.” The lookout reported, “The messenger reached them, but he has not returned.”
The lookout reported, “The messenger reached them, but he has not returned. The driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives furiously.”
“When this letter reaches you, your masters’ sons are with you, and you have chariots, horses, fortified towns, and weapons.”

He went from there and found Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. He greeted him and said to him, “Is your heart as sincere toward me as my heart is toward you?” Jehonadab said, “Yes, it is indeed.” He said to him, “Give me your hand.” He gave him his hand, and he brought him up beside him into the chariot.
Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, “Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him a great deal.”

In the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest sent for the commanders of hundreds, the runners, and the guards, and brought them to him in the house of the Lord. He stationed them in the house of the Lord, made a covenant with them, exchanged oaths with them, and showed them the king’s son.

The commanders of hundreds did as Jehoiada the priest had commanded them. Each man took his men, those coming on duty on the Sabbath together with those going off duty on the Sabbath, and they came to Jehoiada the priest.
They brought out the king’s son and placed the crown of testimony on his head. They anointed him and made him king, clapped their hands, and said, “Long live the king!”
In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash began to reign, and he reigned for forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zoba, from Beersheba.
Joash’s servants rose up in rebellion and killed Joash at Beth Millo as he was going down to Sela.
Jehoahaz prayed before the Lord, and the Lord heard him, because he saw the distress of Israel, whom the king of Edom was oppressing.
He followed the ways of the kings of Israel. He even made his son pass through fire, according to the customs of the nations whom the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites.
They feared the LORD and served their own gods according to the customs of the nations, and the Israelites went into exile from their land.
Hezekiah gave all the silver that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasury of the royal palace.
Look, I will put a spirit in him, and he will hear news and return to his own land. I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.
This is what you must say to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you when you say that Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.
Hezekiah prayed before the LORD and said, “Mighty LORD, God of Israel, enthroned upon the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.”
Therefore, this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow there. He will not advance against it with shields or set ambushes against it.
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “What is the sign that the LORD will heal me and that I will go up to the house of the LORD on the third day?”
Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the LORD.”
Hezekiah died and rested with his ancestors, and his son Manasseh reigned after him.
I will abandon the remnant of my inheritance and hand them over to their enemies. They will become plunder and be trampled by all their enemies.

Shaphan the scribe came to the king to report to him and said, “Your servants have handed over the silver found in the house and delivered it to the workers appointed over the work in the house of the LORD.”

Because your heart softened and you trembled before the LORD when you heard what I said about this place and its inhabitants—that it would become an object of horror and a curse—and you tore your clothes and wept before me, I too have heard, says the LORD.
Josiah also removed all the shrines at the high places in the towns of Samaria that the kings of Israel had built to provoke the LORD to anger. He did to them just as he had done at Bethel.
He slaughtered all the priests of the high places who offered incense on the altars, and he burned human bones on them. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
Pharaoh the Lame made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of his father Josiah and changed his name to Jehoiakim. He took Jehoahaz away, and he went to Egypt and died there.

The LORD stirred up against him raiding bands of Chaldeans, raiding bands of Edom, raiding bands of Moab, and raiding bands of Ammonites. He stirred them up against Judah to destroy them, according to the word of the LORD that he had spoken through his servants the prophets.
At that time Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against Jerusalem, and the city was besieged.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
The city remained under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, deported the rest of the people who remained in the city, the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the remainder of the army, and took them to Babylon.
He changed out of his prison clothes and ate regularly in the king’s presence all the days of his life.
